decisions.rationale: Lead Tyranitar + Excadrill: uncontested Smooth Rock sand gives Excadrill ~236 Speed, outrunning Noivern/Mega Gardevoir, with High Horsepower 81-139% on Kingambit and 4x on H-Arcanine, plus chip on Gardevoir/Milotic/Noivern/Farigiraf. Back Gholdengo (Good as Gold, Normal-immune, Make It Rain 84-144% on Mega Gardevoir, resists Fairy/Psychic) and Sinistcha (Rage Powder to shield Excadrill, Heatproof, Normal-immune, Trick Room to answer Farigiraf, Matcha Gotcha on Milotic/Arcanine).
decisions.notebook:
Game 1 brought: Tyranitar + Excadrill lead, Gholdengo + Sinistcha back (Rotom-Heat, Mega Floette benched; no Mega used G1).
Key verified numbers: Excadrill LO High Horsepower vs Kingambit 80.7-139.4% (roll for OHKO). Gholdengo Wise Glasses Make It Rain single-target vs Mega Gardevoir 84-144% (likely OHKO; spread hit weaker).
Opponent notes: Farigiraf has Armor Tail (blocks our priority moves aimed at their side; Protect/Rage Powder still fine) + Trick Room + Colbur Berry. Noivern max Speed 192 -> sand-rushed Excadrill (~236) outspeeds; Noivern Tailwind is their main speed swing. H-Arcanine Intimidate on switch-in/lead cuts Tyranitar/Excadrill Attack; Head Smash 80% acc, Expert Belt. Milotic Competitive: avoid stat drops (Make It Rain SpA drop only self). Mega Gardevoir Pixilate turns Hyper Voice into Fairy spread; Gholdengo/Excadrill/Tyranitar handle it, Sinistcha does not.
Future games: consider Rotom-Heat over Sinistcha if Kingambit+Arcanine core leads (Overheat/Will-O-Wisp, Levitate); Mega Floette only for slow grind games with sand off. Sinistcha and Rotom take sand chip; Gholdengo/Ttar/Exca don't.
General: keep sand up 8 turns via Smooth Rock; don't let Tyranitar eat Head Smash/Aura Sphere unnecessarily.

decisions.rationale: Lead Gardevoir+Farigiraf for Trick Room to flip Excadrill's Sand Rush speed. Gardevoir Protects T1 while Farigiraf sets TR. Kingambit cleans under TR; Noivern provides Tailwind backup if TR fails or expires. Farigiraf's Armor Tail blocks priority, Colbur Berry helps survive Tyranitar Crunch. Aura Sphere 4x deletes TTar, Mystical Fire roasts Gholdengo.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 lead: Gardevoir+Farigiraf, back Kingambit+Noivern. Plan: T1 Gardevoir Protect + Farigiraf Trick Room. Under TR, Gardevoir Pixilate Hyper Voice sweeps; Farigiraf Psychic/Hyper Voice supports. Aura Sphere OHKOs Tyranitar (75-132%). Mystical Fire 2HKOes Gholdengo. Kingambit Kowtow Cleave threatens Gholdengo (2x). Noivern Tailwind as backup speed control. Threat: Excadrill Iron Head OHKOs Gardevoir (207-296%) — must Protect T1. Farigiraf at risk of double-target KO before TR goes up.

decisions.rationale: Excadrill Iron Head OHKOs Gardevoir (118-234%) even if it Megas (Mega loses Sand Rush, so 236 sand-rushed Excadrill moves first). Tyranitar Crunch on Farigiraf pops Colbur Berry and chips ~30-50% through it, setting up a clean Crunch KO on their Trick Room setter later, and stays useful even if Gardevoir Protects. Protect on Tyranitar would be pure tempo loss; trading Tyranitar for Gardevoir if Aura Sphere connects is acceptable.

reflections.summary: The opponent's Sand Rush Excadrill and Tyranitar lead overwhelmed our team. Farigiraf was unable to set Trick Room safely and was KO'd early, leaving us without speed control. Noivern was a poor lead matchup, being weak to Rock Slide. Kingambit's Sucker Punch was blocked by Excadrill's Protect, and Tyranitar's Low Kick KO'd Kingambit. Gardevoir-Mega was then outsped and KO'd by Excadrill's Iron Head.
reflections.adjustment: For game 2, bring a Ground-resistant or immune Pokemon instead of Noivern to better handle Excadrill. Lead with Farigiraf and a Fake Out user (if available) to safely set Trick Room, or lead with Farigiraf and Kingambit, using Protect on Kingambit turn 1 while Farigiraf sets Trick Room. If keeping Noivern, consider a redirector to set Tailwind, but beware Rock Slide.
reflections.notebook: Game 1: Opponent led Tyranitar (Smooth Rock, Sand Stream, Crunch, Rock Slide, Low Kick, Protect) + Excadrill (Life Orb, Sand Rush, High Horsepower, Iron Head, Rock Slide, Protect). Tyranitar has Low Kick for heavy targets. Excadrill used Protect to block Sucker Punch. Opponent used double Protect effectively. Backline not revealed, but available: Gholdengo (WiseGlasses), Rotom-Heat (Sitrus), Sinistcha (Leftovers, Heatproof), Floette-Eternal (Floettite, Flower Veil). Farigiraf's Colbur Berry consumed early, likely from Tyranitar's Crunch. Noivern is too frail against Rock Slide. For game 2, expect similar lead. Plan: Bring a Ground resist/immunity; prioritize setting Trick Room with Farigiraf + support; consider Kingambit as a Trick Room sweeper but watch for Low Kick; Gardevoir-Mega needs protection from Excadrill's Iron Head.
